findings.description: Appending unversioned rows directly to main.listed bypasses the arm_map provenance validation in Analysis._classify.
findings.failure_mode: With two suite versions present, an unversioned smoke-batch row whose arm disagrees with its manifest's arm_map is now accepted and listed. The report succeeds despite a provenance conflict, which is documented to require exit 2. Versioned smoke rows still undergo this validation.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate manifest arm_map agreement for every row before partitioning, or apply the same provenance check to unversioned rows before appending them to the primary version's listed rows.

findings.description: list_reason() deliberately omits the manifest arm_map provenance check that Analysis._classify runs before any listing decision. partition() now uses list_reason() to accept version-less rows (among 2+ versions) that would be listed anyway, so such a row never reaches _classify. A versioned row in a smoke batch (or with a not-run arm / unknown task type) whose manifest arm_map names a different arm still exits 2 as a provenance conflict; the identical row without a suite_version is now listed with reason 'no suite_version; smoke batch …' and the report exits 0. Before this change every version-less row among two versions exited 2, so the provenance conflict was never silently swallowed.
findings.failure_mode: A provenance conflict (row arm disagrees with manifest arm_map) on a version-less row is not reported; the header's 'exit 2 on provenance conflict' contract is not honoured for this class of rows, and the listed line names an arm the manifest contradicts.
findings.suggested_fix: In partition(), before calling list_reason(), apply the same arm_map check (raise Fail when mans[batch]['arm_map'][run_id] != row['arm']); or move the check into list_reason() so both call sites share it.

findings.description: version_key() now yields non-integer numeric keys ('2.1') that previously could not occur. The diff routes only the top-level primary_suite_version through the new version_value() helper; the other JSON emitters of a version key that the header documents (by_suite_version[N].suite_version, h1.suite_version, a4.suite_version, batches[].suite_version, and version_json()) are not shown and presumably still use the old `int(v) if v.isdigit() else v` idiom or a raw string. For a key like '2.1' they would emit a string while primary_suite_version emits a float. AR-38 compares `jq -r .primary_suite_version` to the text '2.1', which passes for either a float or a string, so the test does not pin the type anywhere.
findings.failure_mode: JSON consumers see primary_suite_version as a float 2.1 but by_suite_version['2.1'].suite_version (and h1/a4) as the string '2.1' or an int-cast failure, breaking equality joins between the top-level block and the per-version block.
findings.suggested_fix: Grep for other emitters of a version key (isdigit()/int(...) on a version string, suite_version fields in version_json, h1/a4, batch_record) and route them through version_value(); add a jq -c / type assertion in AR-38 (e.g. `jq '.primary_suite_version|type'` == number and the same for by_suite_version["2.1"].suite_version).

findings.description: The header now states the batch record is 'Never fatal' and that 'neither aborts the report'. The diff guards batch_status(), grader_tally() and render_batches(), but `recs = batch_record(mans, rows)` remains a bare call outside the new try block in build(). Any exception in batch_record()'s own body (grouping rows by batch, manifest/path lookup, computing the batch's suite_version or directory) still propagates and aborts the whole report, including the decision sections it is documented not to affect.
findings.failure_mode: A malformed manifest field or unexpected row shape in the presentation-only batch record aborts the report with a traceback instead of printing 'Not rendered (…)'.
findings.suggested_fix: Move `recs = batch_record(mans, rows)` inside the same try block as render_batches(), so a failure anywhere in the batch record degrades to the 'Not rendered (…)' section.

findings.description: Two attribution edges changed silently. (1) The old tally matched a run directory by `mm.group(1) == task_id and int(mm.group(2)) == trial` (numeric trial compare); run_dir_of() now compares the formatted string `f'{task}-t{trial}'` and uses `base in names`, so a zero-padded directory such as rc-01-t01 no longer matches and is counted as 'no run dir' / n/a. (2) When a row has rerun directories but none carries the row's run_id in meta/pipeline.json and none holds a grade.json, and the base <task>-t<n> directory is absent, run_dir_of() returns None and the row increments run_dirs_missing, although directories for that trial do exist; the rendered 'no run dir ×N' then overstates missing directories.
findings.failure_mode: Grader-version tallies and run_dirs_missing drift from reality for batches with zero-padded trial names or with interrupted-only reruns; presentation only, no decision impact.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the numeric trial comparison (int(mm.group(2)) == int(r['trial'])) when collecting reruns and when locating the base directory; and either return the highest rerun directory as a last fallback (so its missing grade counts as n/a without incrementing run_dirs_missing) or rename/document run_dirs_missing as 'rows with no attributable directory'.
